To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) optimistic locking can be implemented efficiently, and is useful for many concurrent workloads; and (ii) CLOCK is a simple and effective LRU approximation for read-intensive workloads, and it is particularly effective in combination with a concurrent cuckoo hashing scheme that is optimized for the characteristics of a cache.

the use of CLOCK for eviction in a networked storage system, in conjunction with a hash table with concurrent cuckoo hashing, can substantially improve memory efficiency and network throughput, and that these improvements are particularly significant for small key-value pair workloads.

the following techniques can improve the performance of a networked key-value store by 2x to 3x: (i) use a compact LRU approximation that does not rely on the full LRU state, (ii) use an optimistic cuckoo hashing scheme, and (iii) use optimistic locking for concurrent updates.

, in many cases, the most effective approach to performance improvement is not to build a new system from scratch, but instead to carefully analyze and improve the performance of existing, widely used systems.
